Title: RCI report on Tabung Haji to be published in full, says Anwar
Article:
SEREMBAN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would not redact any part of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH).
He said the report would be published in full, including all recommendations and processes undertaken, with its scope extended beyond the original period covered to examine developments after 2020.
"Following the Cabinet deliberation, the Cabinet was also of the view that the scope should be extended.
"We want to know precisely what happened afterwards and the measures taken by various committees, including the current Lembaga Tabung Haji.
"We have decided to publish the report in its entirety. We will not remove or redact any aspect of the report," he said after performing Friday prayers at Masjid Kariah Paroi Jaya here today.
Anwar said the RCI report itself covered developments from 2014, when Bank Negara Malaysia first issued an early warning.
"Then there was another warning in 2017. The inquiry covered that period, but we have also requested that the investigation include subsequent developments.
"I think it is better that Muslims and all Malaysians are allowed to see the complete picture.
"The most important thing is that it serves as a lesson."
Anwar added that those responsible must be investigated and, where warranted, prosecuted through the proper legal process

Title: Negri polls: 87 reports received, 23 probe papers opened
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police received 87 reports and opened 23 investigation papers involving alleged election offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan Election from July 18 until yesterday.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 761 of 787 permit applications submitted for ceramah and political campaign activities during the period were approved.
"All political programmes and activities are monitored to ensure they comply with the law and do not disrupt public safety and order," he said in a statement today.
Alzafny said police would continue to strengthen preparedness and enforcement efforts, adding that any violation of the law would be dealt with firmly and fairly.
He urged the public to comply with the law, respect the democratic process and cooperate with police to ensure the election is conducted peacefully and orderly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Drugged Malaysian pilot risks death penalty for smuggling in Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTA: A Malaysian pilot who tested positive for meth, MDMA, and cocaine after flying a passenger plane to Indonesia risks the death penalty for allegedly smuggling more than 70,000 ecstasy tablets in his suitcase, officials said Friday.
The 39-year-old pilot, identified only by his initials, MSO, was arrested Wednesday at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta international airport shortly after arriving from Kuala Lumpur.
The airport customs office did not say which carrier the pilot worked for, but the flight number indicated it was a Malaysia Airlines plane.
"The results of his urine test came back positive for meth, MDMA, and cocaine. So, at the time of the flight, he was under the influence," Hengky Tomuan Parlindungan Aritonang, an official at the airport customs office, told reporters in the Indonesian capital.
"What concerns all of us is that this person's profession is a pilot, and at the time he arrived, he had just flown that plane from Kuala Lumpur to Indonesia," he said.
Customs officials found 14 bags of ecstasy – more than 70,000 pills – in the pilot's suitcase, and four grams of meth, thought to be for personal use, in his hand luggage.
Hengky said the pilot likely did not expect to be checked in the special customs lane for pilots and crew, "but the monitoring we carry out is the same" for everyone.
In a statement to investigators, the man said this was the third time he had attempted to smuggle drugs, the second to Indonesia and once in Malaysia.
Awaludin said the police suspected "MSO" to be part of an international syndicate, and he has been charged with smuggling.
Under Indonesian law, he risks the death penalty or life imprisonment.
Indonesia has some of the world's toughest anti-drug laws, including the death penalty for traffickers, but has maintained a moratorium on executions for several years.
Airline 'internal review'
The pilot told investigators he had been promised some RM50,000 (just over US$12,000) to deliver the narcotics in Jakarta.
Malaysia Airlines, in a statement Friday, said it took the allegations seriously and had launched an internal review.
"Malaysia Airlines will extend its full cooperation to the relevant authorities in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations," it said.
The carrier declined further comment pending the Indonesian investigation.
There are dozens of foreign traffickers on death row in Indonesia, hundreds altogether.
The Muslim-majority Southeast Asian country last carried out the death sentence for drug offences in 2016, when one Indonesian and three Nigerians were executed by firing squad.
Two British men were sentenced in March to nine and 11 years in prison, respectively, after they were found guilty of smuggling cocaine onto the tourist island of Bali.
In June, the Bali police arrested two Russian nationals for attempting to smuggle nearly eight kilograms of hashish to the resort island.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Riyadh Air launches thrice weekly Riyadh-Kuala Lumpur flight
Article:
SEPANG: Riyadh Air has launched a three-times-weekly flight between Riyadh and Kuala Lumpur, making the Malaysian capital its first destination in Southeast Asia.
Riyadh Air chief executive officer Tony Douglas said Kuala Lumpur represented an important step in the airline's international expansion.
"Today's inaugural flight to Kuala Lumpur is a defining moment for Riyadh Air as we establish our footprint in Southeast Asia.
"This route is far more than a direct connection between two capital cities, as it builds a vital bridge between Saudi Arabia and the broader Asean region."
"By facilitating seamless travel for business, tourism, and education, we are actively supporting Vision 2030 while delivering an elevated, digitally led travel experience for our guests," he said in a statement.
The route was developed in partnership with Saudi Arabia's air connectivity programme, which supports the kingdom's aviation and tourism development plans.
Riyadh Air said the Malaysia-Saudi Arabia market is a mature intercontinental corridor supported by year-round demand from corporate travel, higher education, leisure tourism and religious travel.
Malaysia Airports managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani said Riyadh Air's decision to select Kuala Lumpur as its first Southeast Asian destination was significant for Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and Malaysia.
"As the ninth Middle Eastern airline to serve KLIA, its entry further strengthens our connectivity with a region that is an increasingly important market for tourism, trade and travel."
"For Malaysia Airports, this is about continuing to build a network that gives passengers greater choice while strengthening KLIA's role as a gateway between Southeast Asia and the rest of the world," he said.
The first Riyadh-Kuala Lumpur nonstop flight departed King Khalid International Airport on July 30, while the first return flight from KLIA Terminal 1 departed on July 31.
The route is operated using the airline's Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner aircraft.
Riyadh Air said its Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners feature four cabin classes comprising Business Elite, Business, Premium Economy and Economy.
The aircraft are equipped with lie-flat seats in Business Elite and Business, as well as power outlets, USB charging ports, Bluetooth audio and Panasonic Avionics' Astrova inflight entertainment system.
Besides Kuala Lumpur, Riyadh Air also flies to London, Jeddah, Cairo, Dubai, Malaga and Madrid.
The airline will also start flying to Dhaka and Mumbai in August 2026.
Riyadh Air, which is wholly owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, aims to serve more than 100 destinations worldwide by 2030.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: North Korea growth topped 3pct for third straight year in 2025: Seoul
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea's economy grew more than three per cent for a third straight year in 2025, South Korea's central bank estimated Friday, as Pyongyang continues to deepen economic and military ties with Russia.
The Bank of Korea (BoK) has published annual estimates of the North's economy since 1991, based on its own intelligence and trade data because Pyongyang does not release official statistics.
The isolated North's real gross domestic product expanded 3.5 per cent to 38.26 trillion (US$26.6 billion) won last year, the Bank of Korea said in its report.
Pyongyang has deepened economic and military ties with Russia, supplying troops and munitions for Moscow's war in Ukraine in exchange for financial support, food, energy and military technology, analysts say.
"The expansion of economic cooperation with Russia was a major driver of North Korea's growth last year," a BoK official told AFP.
Higher weapons exports to Russia boosted related manufacturing, while more Russian tourists and expanded transport links lifted construction and services, she added.
More than 7,000 North Korean troops were killed or wounded while fighting alongside Russian forces in the Kursk region during the 2024-2025 campaign, the Kyiv Independent quoted Ukraine's military intelligence agency as saying.
The BoK said North Korea's exports rose 30 per cent last year to US$470 million, driven by "prepared feathers and wigs", as well as unspecified toys and sporting goods.
The BoK estimate came as Ukrainian rights group Truth Hounds claimed Russia and North Korea were close to completing their first road bridge, citing their own investigation.
The bridge could become "a direct artery for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, with Russian technology and resources flowing in the opposite direction", the group said in its report.
The BoK official said North Korea's gross national income also "received a boost from a sharp rise in foreign currency earnings" linked to the deployment of its troops to Russia.
GNI -- the total income earned by all residents -- rose rose 9.4 per cent to 48.5 trillion won (US$33.8 billion) last year. That amounts to less than two per cent of South Korea's, according to the BoK report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines conducting internal review after pilot arrested in Indonesia over drugs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines is conducting an internal review after a pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities over alleged narcotics-related offences.
The national carrier, however, declined to comment on the arrest of the pilot, who was reportedly found with more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, but said it takes such allegations seriously.
In a statement to Bernama today, Malaysia Airlines said it would not be appropriate to comment further as the matter remains under investigation by the Indonesian authorities.
The airline said it would cooperate with the relevant authorities in accordance with all applicable laws and regulations.
"Malaysia Airlines wishes to reiterate that it does not tolerate any form of misconduct and is conducting an internal review into the matter," it said.
The airline added that the safety, security and integrity of its operations remained its priority.
According to Indonesian Customs and Excise director-general Djaka Budi Utama, the pilot is under investigation for allegedly attempting to traffic drugs, including ecstasy worth about 60 billion rupiah (RM14 million), into Indonesia.
It was reported that the 39-year-old
suspect had operated
Malaysia Airlines flight MH727 from Kuala Lumpur to Jakarta before he was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport on Wednesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Armed forces chief: Honour national heroes, instil patriotism in future generations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Armed Forces Chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman has called on Malaysians to uphold patriotism and continue honouring the sacrifices of national heroes who defended the country's independence, sovereignty and peace.
He said appreciation for the contributions of servicemen and women must be strengthened to ensure their sacrifices are never forgotten and continue to inspire future generations to safeguard the nation's security and prosperity.
In conjunction with National Warriors' Day 2026 today, Malek extended his greetings to all Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel, including serving members, veterans and the families of those who died or were killed in the line of duty.
"Today is a manifestation of our appreciation for all national heroes and MAF members who have sacrificed so much to secure and preserve our independence.
"It is a reminder to present and future generations that respect and gratitude for our national heroes must remain firmly embedded in the hearts of all Malaysians in recognition of their invaluable sacrifices," he told reporters after attending the National Warriors' Day 2026 parade here today.
Held under the theme Mengenang Jasa, Mengukuh Pertahanan (Honouring Service, Strengthening Defence), the parade, organised by the army, paid tribute to members of the nation's security forces who served during the Emergency and Confrontation eras, while highlighting that peace and stability were achieved through immense sacrifice.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, attended the ceremony.
Also present were Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families seek legal action over Sungai Pari Flats deaths
Article:
IPOH: The families of two schoolgirls who died after falling from the abandoned Sungai Pari Flats in Buntong last week are seeking legal action against parties they claim failed to ensure the safety of the premises.
The families of the two girls, both aged 14, alleged that the lack of proper security measures, including the absence of fencing around the 15-storey abandoned building, had exposed the public, including children, to danger.
Their families said they believed negligence had contributed to the tragedy involving their daughters, who were close friends.
The two girls were found dead at the abandoned flats on July 24, believed to have fallen from the building.
Speaking after lodging a police report at Buntong Police Station here today, the grieving fathers said they wanted those responsible to be held accountable and for measures to be taken to prevent a similar tragedy.
"We are deeply disappointed that parties who should have been responsible appeared to have failed to take follow-up action.
"Our intention in lodging this report is to ensure that such an incident does not happen again and that appropriate measures are taken for public safety," they said.
The fathers, accompanied by about 20 family members during a peaceful gathering outside the police station, said they had appointed lawyers and intended to pursue the matter through legal channels.
They added that investigations into the deaths of both girls would be left entirely to police.
The families also called for immediate measures, including installing proper fencing around the abandoned flats, increasing police patrols and deploying more security personnel to monitor the area.
"There are 12 blocks in the area, yet only one security guard is assigned to monitor the premises, including the 15th floor.
"If the demolition process takes time, we urge the Ipoh City Council (MBI) to immediately fence off the entire area as the site belongs to the state government," they said.
The Sungai Pari Flats, also known as Sungai Pari Tower or Tingkat 15, is set to be demolished as part of a redevelopment plan, with a developer already appointed for the project.
However, Perak Housing and Property Board chief executive officer Zaiteena Wan Nasir said the
demolition could not be carried out
immediately as several procedures, including obtaining planning permission from MBI and rezoning approval, must first be completed.
Built in 1963, the 15-storey public housing project was once an iconic landmark in Ipoh and among the tallest structures in the city.
The building was gradually vacated from 2012 due to concerns over its structural condition and has remained abandoned since then.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: ITMAX secures RM120mil DBKL smart lighting contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: ITMAX System Bhd has secured a RM120 million contract from Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to supply, install and maintain smart street lighting systems across Kuala Lumpur.
The artificial intelligence (AI)-powered integrated digital infrastructure service provider said the six-year contract will run from Aug 1, 2026, to July 31, 2032.
ITMAX System managing director and chief executive officer William Tan Wei Lun said the award reflected DBKL's continued confidence in the group's capabilities and proven track record.
"This award also recognises our locally designed and developed Malaysian smart street lighting system, demonstrating that home-grown innovation can deliver world-class smart city solutions.
"Our intelligent street lighting platform incorporates features such as adaptive dimming, centralised monitoring and real-time fault detection to improve energy efficiency, operational reliability and public safety," he said in a statement.
Tan said the company remains committed to developing AI-powered technologies that support Malaysia's digital transformation and help build smarter, safer and more sustainable cities.

Title: Govt shifts focus to scaling up MSMEs after resilient 2025
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) have weathered global uncertainties well, with the government's focus now shifting to helping more firms grow beyond the micro stage, the Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Ministry said.
Despite outpacing the broader economy in 2025, more than three quarters of MSMEs remained micro enterprises, highlighting the need to help businesses scale up, improve productivity and expand into international markets, Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said.
He said ongoing geopolitical conflicts, tariffs and higher energy costs have disrupted global supply chains, making it more difficult and costly for businesses to obtain raw materials and other supplies.es.
"Geopolitical tensions will certainly affect our country. Beyond higher prices, supply chains and accessibility are also affected.
"Businesses are not only facing higher costs but are sometimes unable to obtain the supplies they need because of wars or geopolitical tensions," he told reporters after announcing Malaysia's 2025 MSME performance at SME Corp Malaysia.
According to the Statistics Department, MSME gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.7 per cent to RM689.8 billion in 2025.
The sector outpaced Malaysia's overall economic growth of 5.2 per cent, with its contribution to GDP increasing to 39.7 per cent from 39.5 per cent in 2024.
Malaysia had nearly 1.3 million MSMEs in 2025, representing 96 per cent of all businesses, almost 20 per cent more than the previous year.
However, Sim said more than 77 per cent remained micro enterprises, while only 1.1 per cent were medium-sized businesses.
He said the government's priority is now to help more MSMEs scale up, improve productivity and expand into international markets.
Despite global headwinds, Sim said Malaysia's MSME sector remained resilient, with export growth demonstrating its adaptability.
MSME exports rose 10.5 per cent to RM214.5 billion in 2025, surpassing overall national export growth of 5.9 per cent and the 5.1 per cent growth recorded by non-MSME firms.
"These crises did not begin this year. Their impact was already felt last year through tariffs, higher energy costs and slowing demand from our trading partners.
"When our trading partners slow down, they buy less from us. Even so, Malaysia's economy remained stable, while MSMEs continued growing faster than the overall economy," Sim added.
To accelerate business scaling, the ministry is implementing the Power Up 10K initiative, backed by RM15 billion in financing.
The initiative aims to strengthen productivity, improve cash flow and enhance business capacity while expanding access to domestic and international markets under the ministry's ABCD strategic framework.
It also supports the government's target of increasing the proportion of medium-sized enterprises to five per cent by 2030.
Sim also witnessed the exchange of memoranda of understanding between SME Corp Malaysia, the Malaysia-China Chamber of Commerce and the Small and Medium Enterprises Association to strengthen collaboration in supporting MSME growth and internationalisation.
The event also saw the launch of a quick guide on utilising free trade agreements (FTAs), designed to help SMEs leverage Malaysia's 17 FTAs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Police confirm Malaysian pilot's arrest in Jakarta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Police have confirmed that a 39-year-old Malaysian pilot was detained by Indonesian authorities for allegedly attempting to smuggle drugs through Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta.
Federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the man was arrested shortly after arriving in Jakarta from Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday night.
"I confirm the arrest. We have been informed. The suspect was detained there and will face action under the laws of that country," he said when contacted.
Earlier, Indonesian media reported that a Malaysian pilot was arrested for allegedly
attempting to smuggle
a large quantity of drugs, including more than 70,000 ecstasy pills weighing 25kg, into Indonesia recently.
()
Reports by Kompas.com and Suara.com said Indonesian authorities also found 2.74g of methamphetamine, as well as 0.0825g of methamphetamine residue in a glass pipe, when the suspect was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta Airport at about 11.30pm local time on Tuesday.
Indonesian Police Narcotics Crime Directorate director Brigadier General Eko Hadi Santoso said Customs officers decided to inspect the suspect's suitcase after detecting something suspicious during an X-ray scan at the international arrivals area.
"Checks showed that officers found 14 large packages containing ecstasy and one packet containing methamphetamine," he was quoted as saying.
Apart from the drugs, he said authorities also seized several items belonging to the suspect, including a backpack, Malaysian passport, Malaysian identity card, Malaysian driving licence, an iPhone and his uniform.
He added that during preliminary investigations, the suspect admitted he had been instructed by an individual to transport the drugs to Jakarta in exchange for RM50,000.
The suspect told investigators that upon arriving in Jakarta, he would be directed by someone believed to be based in Malaysia, and that another person would collect the items at a hotel or accommodation.
The suspect also told investigators that he had acted as a drug courier three times.
The first involved transporting methamphetamine to Sabah, Malaysia.
The second involved smuggling 7kg of methamphetamine into Jakarta.
The third involved transporting ecstasy and methamphetamine, which was foiled by officers at Soekarno-Hatta Airport.
A urine test showed that the suspect tested positive for methamphetamine, MDMA and cocaine.
The suspect is being detained at the Bareskrim Polri detention centre to assist investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EV charging network must grow with adoption, says Johari
Article:
TANJUNG MALIM: The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry will team up with Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and other relevant parties to strengthen Malaysia's electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure as adoption of the technology accelerates.
Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the government is determined to ensure the country's EV ecosystem develops in tandem with vehicle sales, as inadequate charging facilities could undermine consumer confidence.
The ministry is targeting 30,000 public EV chargers nationwide, although no timeline has been set. Johari said Malaysia currently has about 1,000 charging stations.
He added that Malaysia has forgone RM3.3 billion in tax revenue over the past four years by exempting imported EVs from import and excise duties, while public charging infrastructure has yet to keep pace.
"Today, EV adoption is mainly concentrated in urban areas. For long-distance travel, we're still a long way from where we need to be because we lack enough public chargers," he said after attending a media preview of the locally assembled Proton e.MAS 7 PHEV here.
Johari said EV adoption remains challenging for many Malaysians, particularly those living in flats and condominiums, as limited charging facilities and inadequate electrical capacity in older buildings make installing home chargers difficult.
"These are the issues we need to address. We are not against EVs. But we should not move ahead of the market before the ecosystem is ready. Ultimately, the problems faced by consumers will become problems for the government," he said.
Johari said the widespread adoption of internal combustion engine vehicles has been supported by Malaysia's network of about 3,500 petrol stations, providing an estimated 35,000 refuelling points nationwide.
"For EVs, the situation is very different. Even where public chargers are available, there may be only one or two, leaving motorists reluctant to travel long distances for fear they may be unable to recharge their vehicles.
"I asked China's trade minister how the country became so successful in promoting EVs. He told me it was because the government invested billions of dollars in public charging infrastructure.
"In Malaysia, however, we have spent billions on tax exemptions instead of investing in charging infrastructure. That is our challenge," he said.
Johari said Malaysia should emulate China's success by investing in EV charging infrastructure while exploring ways to generate revenue from growing EV adoption to fund further infrastructure development.
"We will also discuss with TNB how it can provide the substations needed to support more public chargers. These are matters that require careful planning.
"The government must look at the entire ecosystem. Otherwise, people will complain. Local authorities and the Housing and Local Government Ministry also need to plan ahead.
"In future public housing projects and flats, we need to determine whether space can be allocated for 10, 20 or even 30 public chargers, depending on the number of parking bays available," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Negri polls: Anwar seeks continuity, stability in election appeal [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim appealed to Negri Sembilan voters to set aside political differences and give the unity government a fresh mandate as campaigning drew to a close ahead of tomorrow's state election.
In a video message posted on his social media platforms today, Anwar said the campaign period may have been marked by "excesses" and called on voters to forgive one another.
"We have gone through the campaign period and presented various views, and I believe that in the process, there are sometimes excesses.
"So let us all apologise to one another and be friends again, because we are competing among fellow Malaysians, the residents of Negri Sembilan," he said.
Anwar also appealed to voters of all backgrounds to fulfil their civic duty.
"To the residents of Negri Sembilan, especially the Muslim majority, and our friends among the Chinese, Indian and Orang Asli communities, let us fulfil our responsibility (to vote)," he said.
He also called on voters to continue supporting PH candidates, saying continuity and political stability were needed to sustain the coalition's achievements over the past two terms.
"If permitted, I, representing Pakatan Harapan, ask to be given the opportunity to continue serving, to guarantee stability and drive growth that will ensure the well-being of all the people of Negri Sembilan," said Anwar.
The Negri Sembilan polls will take place tomorrow, Aug 1, with PH contesting all 36 seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: QR code immigration clearance system expands to 4 Sarawak border posts
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry, in collaboration with the Sarawak government, will expand the MyNIISe QR code immigration clearance system to four major border checkpoints along the Sarawak-Brunei border starting tomorrow.
The initiative marks the latest expansion of Malaysia's border management digital transformation, following successful rollouts at KLIA Terminals 1 and 2, the Sultan Iskandar Building and Sultan Abu Bakar Complex in Johor, as well as Kuching International Airport.
"The system aims to expedite immigration checks, boost service efficiency and reinforce national border security," the Home Ministry said in a statement.
It said the QR code clearance system would cover vehicle lanes across four key border posts, namely the Sungai Tujoh, Tedungan, Pandaruan and Mengkalap Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) complexes.
A total of six QR code reader units have been installed at each checkpoint, with three for outgoing lanes and three for incoming lanes, to ensure smoother processing and alleviate traffic congestion during peak hours.
The ministry said the land border rollout marks the second phase of the NIISe implementation in Sarawak.
The first phase, launched at Kuching International Airport on April 23, has recorded 11,851 smooth departure clearances to date.
It also said the MyNIISe application had gained strong traction among travellers since its launch on September 22 last year.
"As of July 26, the application has recorded more than 2.5 million downloads, with over 1.3 million registered users.
"Overall, the NIISe platform has logged 30.36 million transactions across the country's main air, land and sea gateways."
The ministry also advised frequent travellers along the Sarawak-Brunei border to download and register on the MyNIISe application early via the Google Play Store, Apple App Store or Huawei AppGallery to ensure faster and smoother border clearance.
It added that the move demonstrated its commitment to strengthening national border security while supporting the nation's overall digital transformation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sultan Nazrin witnesses poignant tribute to Al-Maunah fallen heroes
Article:
IPOH: The courage, sacrifice and unwavering commitment of Malaysia's security personnel during the Al-Maunah crisis were brought to life through a poignant pantomime titled Operasi Subuh.
The performance was witnessed by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah, during the state-level Warriors' Day celebration here today.
The performance revisited one of the country's most challenging security episodes — the 2000 armed standoff involving the Al-Maunah militant group, which claimed the lives of two security personnel.
The crisis began on July 2, 2000, when 15 men disguised as military personnel entered the 304th Malaysian Army camp in Gerik, claiming they were conducting an inspection.
Within two hours, the group escaped with a large cache of weapons, including M16 and AUG rifles, GPMG machine guns, ammunition and communication equipment.
The stolen weapons were later taken to Bukit Jenalik in Sauk, Kuala Kangsar, where members of the Al-Maunah group camped, triggering a major security operation involving the Malaysian Armed Forces and police.
The pantomime depicted the unfolding of events after Lieutenant General (Rtd) Datuk Seri Zaini Mohamad Said received an urgent call from Second Division Commander Major General Datuk Khairuddin Mat Yusof over the security breach.
The situation escalated the following day after military personnel intercepted radio communications from the group, with Al-Maunah members claiming they were holding hostages.
Among the most emotional scenes was the portrayal of the sacrifices made by 21st Special Service member Trooper Matthew Medan and Kuala Kangsar district police headquarters officer Detective Corporal R. Sanghadevan.
As the standoff continued, security forces launched psychological operations on July 4 to persuade the militants to surrender.
Messages from family members were used to appeal to the emotions of the group members, prompting several to attempt to leave the hideout. However, their attempts were reportedly stopped by group leader Mohamed Amin Mohamed Razali.
The following day, another exchange of gunfire between security forces and the militants resulted in the death of one Al-Maunah member.
Security forces continued applying pressure through controlled operations, including firing into the air at intervals to prevent the group from resting, eventually forcing several members to surrender.
By the morning of July 6, seven more Al-Maunah members had surrendered, providing crucial information that helped authorities bring the operation to an end.
Security forces were tasked with four key objectives: securing the militants' surrender without further loss of life, recovering the stolen weapons, rescuing hostages and completing the mission before nightfall.
In a final attempt to end the standoff peacefully, Zaini met Mohamed Amin personally. The encounter ended with security forces overpowering and detaining the Al-Maunah members.
In August 2006, Mohamed Amin was sentenced to death at Sungai Buloh Prison, Selangor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration hack: Insiders exploited to breach MyIMMs system
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The syndicate suspected of hacking the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to unlawfully process Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) applications exploited insiders within the Immigration Department to gain access to the system.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation, uncovered under Op Crack, could not have been carried out without the involvement of people familiar with the department's systems.
"Penetrating the MyIMMs system from outside is not possible. We recently conducted forensic checks with CyberSecurity Malaysia to strengthen system security.
"It could not be breached externally. In this case, it involved insiders who understood the system," he told a press conference at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) headquarters today.
Zakaria said the suspects used dongle devices and software installed on computers to gain access before using administrator login credentials to create fake accounts and approve PLKS applications fraudulently.
Op Crack followed intelligence sharing between the MACC and the Immigration Department in May, with raids launched on July 28.
The operation involved the MACC, Immigration Department, Securities Commission Malaysia, Telekom Malaysia, National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa) and the MACC Technology Forensics Division.
Twelve people were remanded until today, including two company directors, three foreigners, six Immigration Department officers and a police officer.
Authorities also seized RM186,360 in cash, SGD700, 19 mobile phones, six laptops, two computers, two CPUs, a router and gold jewellery and bullion worth an estimated RM15,700.
The MACC is also moving to freeze bank accounts belonging to people and companies linked to the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2 Filipinos jailed for illegal entry after murder probe detention
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Two Filipino men detained in connection with the investigation into the murder of a 10-year-old girl were each jailed for four months after pleading guilty to entering Sabah illegally.
Sessions Court Judge Hurman Hussain meted out the sentence to the two men, aged 39 and 21.
The court also ordered both men to be referred to the Immigration Department for further action after serving their prison sentences.
The 39-year-old was arrested at about 2.30pm on July 16, 2026, at an open area in Kampung Numbak 2, Manggatal.
The 21-year-old was arrested three days later, at about 3.20pm on July 19, by the roadside in Kampung Numbak, Sepanggar.
Investigations found that neither man possessed a valid pass or permit required by law to enter Sabah.
They were convicted under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, punishable under Section 6(3) of the same Act, which carries a fine of up to RM10,000, imprisonment of up to five years, or both, as well as up to six strokes of the cane.
Prosecuting Officer Inspector Deanivo Sittin prosecuted the case, while the two men were unrepresented.
The 39-year-old had previously been remanded alongside a 42-year-old local man after they were detained following the discovery of the
body of 10-year-old Nurjilya Abdullah
in a bushy area near a house under construction in Kampung Numbak, Sepanggar, on July 16.
Their remand, which began on July 17, was extended until July 31 to
allow police
to complete their investigation.

Title: EC: No official complaints over vote-buying in Negri polls
Article:
TAMPIN: The Election Commission (EC) has not received any official complaints over allegations of vote-buying or bribery during early voting or the Negri Sembilan election campaign, says chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun.
He urged anyone with information to lodge reports with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) or the police, as such offences fall under their jurisdiction.
"We have not received any official complaints regarding bribery. We hope those with information will report the matter directly to MACC or the police.
"We only receive reports on minor election offences, and appropriate action has been taken," he told reporters after inspecting preparations at the official vote counting centre at Dewan Perdana Tampin today.
Ramlan said the EC had recorded 267 election offences since campaigning began on July 18, with action taken in each case.
He said that all polling centres across Negri Sembilan were ready to receive voters from 8am tomorrow.
"Based on our inspections, everything is in place and we are confident the voting process will proceed smoothly," he added.
Ramlan said the results were expected as early as 10pm, with the full outcome likely before midnight.
A total of 15,344 election officials have been deployed to oversee polling involving 859,760 registered voters, including 7,391 postal voters, across 36 state seats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prosecute those implicated in Tabung Haji RCI report, says consumer association
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has urged the authorities to prosecute those implicated in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
Its president, Mohideen Abdul Kader, said the declassified RCI report exposed governance failures, political interference and financial misrepresentation that amounted to a betrayal of millions of depositors.
"The findings confirmed longstanding concerns that the pilgrim fund had been subjected to political influence and 'creative accounting', undermining public confidence in one of Malaysia's most important Islamic institutions," he said in a statement today.
Mohideen said the report had also damaged Malaysia's international standing as a leader in Islamic finance, noting that TH had long been regarded as a model for pilgrimage fund management and Islamic social finance.
He said the RCI found that while TH reported a RM3.4 billion profit in 2017, proper financial reporting standards showed the fund had actually recorded a RM1.4 billion net loss, reflecting a RM4.8 billion discrepancy.
According to the report, TH had been operating with an asset-liability deficit since 2014 but continued paying hibah beyond its financial capacity, while bonuses were allegedly paid to executives and board members despite the fund's financial position.
Mohideen said the RCI identified political interference as the root cause of the governance failures, with key decisions on hibah distributions and investments allegedly influenced by political considerations rather than sound financial management.
"As such, CAP calls on the Attorney-General's Chambers and the MACC to prosecute all individuals found to have abused their positions or breached public trust, regardless of their status.
"We also call for amendments to the Tabung Haji Act to reduce ministerial powers, prohibit active politicians from serving on the fund's board or management, and strengthen regulatory oversight of its investment operations," he added.
The
Cabinet had previously agreed to declassify
and release the report, which examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
Among its key findings, the RCI said
TH should have recorded a RM1.4 billion loss
in 2017 instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported in its financial statements after accounting for impairment losses and other financial adjustments.
It also highlighted governance weaknesses, including broad ministerial powers over appointments, overlapping roles among directors and senior management, and concerns over political influence.
The commission
recommended strengthening TH's governance
framework by introducing clearer criteria for board appointments, limiting active politicians from holding board positions and enhancing oversight mechanisms.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today
began investigations
into the RCI report by sending an eight-member team to TH's headquarters to identify documents related to the findings, recommendations and other materials relevant to the probe.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib questions selective trust in National Audit Department over TH issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Najib Razak today questioned what he described as selective judgement towards the National Audit Department over issues surrounding its findings on Tabung Haji (TH).
In a Facebook post, the former prime minister questioned whether the department's findings should only be trusted when they aligned with the position of the government of the day.
"This involves a serious institutional question.
"Do we still trust the National Audit Department, or do we only trust it when its findings are favourable to the government in power?"
In the same post, Najib also shared a social media post by former Barisan Nasional strategic communications deputy director Datuk Eric See-To, who questioned the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on TH and the Auditor General's decision to issue unqualified audit opinions on the fund's financial statements.
See-To said the RCI itself acknowledged that TH's financial statements for 2014 to 2017 were issued with unqualified audit opinions by the National Audit Department.
However, he said that following the change of government, private audit firm PricewaterhouseCoopers Malaysia Holdings Sdn Bhd (PwC) was engaged to review TH's financial position using different approaches, parameters and valuation assumptions.
"Suddenly, accounts that had previously reflected a surplus were presented as showing a RM4.1 billion deficit.
"This raises several questions. Why was the National Audit Department's acceptance of TH's asset valuation methods considered problematic?
"Yet when a private audit firm used different assumptions and valuation methods, why was its conclusion accepted as the absolute truth?
"Is a private audit firm always more accurate than the country's highest auditing institution?" he asked.
See-To said that if the National Audit Department had indeed been negligent or wrong, those responsible should be held accountable.
"Were the officers who approved the unqualified audit opinions ever subjected to any action?" he asked.
The RCI, in its report on Wednesday
found that TH's accounts
should not have received a clean audit opinion as they contained significant accounting issues, including the failure to recognise impairment losses and reflect the true value of certain assets.
Among the issues highlighted were the failure to recognise impairment losses involving investments in subsidiaries, associated companies and debt instruments, as well as the recording of dividend income that had not been received.
The commission found that if these adjustments had been properly reflected in accordance with Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS), TH would have recorded a RM1.4 billion net loss for the 2017 financial year instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Real Property Development Act in final drafting stage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A proposed Real Property Development Act is in the final stage of drafting as part of efforts to strengthen regulation of Malaysia's property sector, says Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said the proposed legislation would expand regulation beyond housing to cover selected commercial property developments while ensuring a fair balance between industry and consumer interests.
"We are aiming to introduce the Real Property Development Act, which is now in the final stage of drafting," he said at the AREC Forum 2026: Rethinking Real Estate: Housing With Hearts today.
Nga said the Act formed part of five housing reforms introduced by the ministry to improve governance and transparency in the property sector.
The reforms also include the electronic sale and purchase agreement (eSPA), the Housing Integrated Management System (HIMS), the National Property Data System and regulated housing development accounts.
He said the measures were aimed at eliminating sick and abandoned housing projects by 2030.
Nga added that more than 95,000 first-time homebuyers had secured financing under the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme, with RM22 billion of the RM40 billion allocation utilised.
The ministry is targeting 100,000 beneficiaries under the scheme, with more than 17 financial institutions participating.
Malaysia's home ownership rate currently stands at 77 per cent, with the government aiming to raise it above 80 per cent.
"A home is not only a shelter, but also a place of refuge for families and a means of wealth creation and preservation," he said.
Also participating in the forum were China's Minister of Housing and Urban-Rural Development Ni Hong and Sime Darby Property Group managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Azmir Merican.
The forum was moderated by United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) executive director Datuk Seri Maimunah Mohd Sharif.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More arrests possible in MyIMMs hacking probe, says MACC chief
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: More people are on the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) radar in its probe into the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to unlawfully process and approve Temporary Employment Visit Pass (PLKS) applications.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the number of people involved could be considered substantial, with investigations ongoing to determine the extent of their involvement.
"The investigation is still ongoing and we expect more arrests and seizures to be carried out with the cooperation of the Immigration Department.
"Two companies are also suspected to be involved in the process of unlawfully applying for and approving PLKS, but their identities cannot be disclosed at this time," he said at a press conference at the MACC headquarters today.
He said Op Crack was initiated following intelligence sharing between the MACC and Immigration Department since May, before the operation was carried out on July 28.
"The operation involved the MACC Intelligence Division's Special Project Branch, together with the Immigration Department Intelligence Division, Securities Commission Malaysia, Telekom Malaysia, National Cyber Security Agency (Nacsa), and the MACC Technology Forensics Division.
"As of now, 12 people have been remanded for between two and three days from July 29 until today to assist investigations," he said.
He said those detained comprised two company directors, three foreign nationals, four Immigration Department officers, two officers from the Immigration Department's Information Technology Division, and a police officer.
"The MACC has also recorded statements from four people and will call several more witnesses to assist investigations," he said.
Halim said the operation also saw the seizure of RM186,360 in cash, foreign currency amounting to SGD700 (RM2,313), 19 mobile phones, six laptops, two computers, two CPUs and a router.
He added that investigators also seized seven gold bars weighing 0.2g each, one two-gram gold bar, a gold chain, a gold bracelet and a gold keychain, with the total value estimated at RM15,700.
The MACC is also in the process of freezing accounts belonging to persons and companies linked to the investigation.
On the remand status of the 12 people, Halim said their remand period would expire today, with the MACC expected to apply for extensions for some of them.
"Their remand ends today. For some, we will apply for an extension, subject to whether the court allows it," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nga: Big data platform to fix housing supply mismatch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Housing and Local Government Ministry is developing a big data analytics platform that will allow private developers to make more informed housing decisions and address the mismatch between supply and market demand.
Minister Nga Kor Ming said developers would eventually be able to subscribe to the platform, allowing feasibility studies to be based on data and actual market needs rather than assumptions.
"Once it is fully implemented, we will open it to the private sector so developers can subscribe to the system. When they come up with a housing scheme, their feasibility studies will be data-driven," he said at the AREC Forum 2026: Rethinking Real Estate: Housing With Hearts today.
Nga said the platform would help ensure housing projects better match buyers' needs, adding that Malaysia's housing sector did not face a supply shortage but a mismatch between available homes and market demand.
The initiative complements existing measures to improve housing accessibility, including the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme, which has helped more than 95,000 homebuyers secure financing.
Nga said the ministry was also studying the housing needs of the M40 income group to ensure future housing products better reflect market requirements.
Meanwhile, the ministry has set up a special task force, chaired by its secretary-general, to review compliance costs faced by developers and streamline requirements without compromising public interest.
"Reducing unnecessary compliance costs would improve project viability without compromising safety and regulatory standards.
"We must safeguard public interest while ensuring the private sector remains commercially viable," he said.
On urban development, Nga said transit-oriented developments (TOD) could eventually be designed without parking bays in areas with comprehensive public transport networks, reducing construction costs and improving affordability.
He said that such an approach could only be adopted once the country's public transport system was sufficiently developed.
The forum was moderated by United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) executive director Datuk Seri Dr Maimunah Mohd Sharif.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign automakers must help build Malaysia's auto ecosystem, says Johari
Article:
TANJUNG MALIM: Foreign automakers investing in Malaysia must go beyond selling vehicles and instead contribute to the development of the country's automotive ecosystem, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said.
The Investment, Trade and Industry Minister said investors should work alongside local entrepreneurs and players to create jobs, strengthen supply chains and generate wider economic benefits.
"They must coexist with the ecosystem that we already have and help build it together with our entrepreneurs and component manufacturers.
"The government also benefits. Today, Proton's tax contribution has reached RM806 million. This comes from corporate tax, excise duty, import duty and sales tax. All these taxes benefit the country.
"This is an industry that creates significant multiplier effects. But this can only happen if we adopt the mindset that investors coming into Malaysia must coexist with existing industries.
"We do not want investments that come here only to displace or undermine businesses that are already operating in the country," Johari told reporters after a media preview of the locally assembled Proton e.MAS 7 PHEV.
Johari said Proton, through its partnership with China's Geely, has evolved into a stronger automotive player with its own intellectual property and advanced manufacturing capabilities.
"For example, Proton previously did not have the opportunity to enhance its production through advanced technologies.
"Geely possessed those technologies and shared them with Proton, with some intellectual property (IP) even being registered in Malaysia. This is what people call a true partnership, not one where a company simply comes here to export cars," he said.
He added that the national carmaker now employs about 9,700 workers and produces more than 150,000 vehicles annually, demonstrating how strategic partnerships help develop domestic industrial capabilities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Coal mine blast kills at least 34 in Pakistan
Article:
QUETTA, Pakistan: A blast at a coal mine killed at least 34 workers in southern Pakistan, the provincial disaster agency said on Friday, adding rescuers were searching for more missing miners.
The explosion, caused by methane gas, tore through the mine near the capital of the resource-rich province of Balochistan on Thursday, sparking a rescue operation that ran into the night.
"According to information received from the deployed teams, 34x Dead bodies have been recovered," southern Balochistan's provincial disaster management authority said in a statement in the early hours of Friday.
"The joint rescue operation is still underway to locate and recover the remaining trapped miners," it added, without specifying how many were in the mine when the explosion took place.
Mining accidents are common in Pakistan, particularly in Balochistan.
Pakistan's poorest province and largest by landmass, Balochistan lags behind the rest of the country in almost every index, including education, employment and economic development.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight arrested over alleged online travel scam targeting China, Taiwan
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Eight foreigners allegedly operating an online travel scam targeting victims in China and Taiwan were arrested after police raided a luxury condominium in Tanjung Bungah yesterday.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the suspects, comprising seven foreign men and a woman aged between 25 and 37, were arrested inside the condominium unit.
Police also seized various computer and telecommunications equipment believed to have been used to operate the fraudulent call centre.
"Initial investigations found the syndicate allegedly offered online travel packages to Japan to victims in China and Taiwan," he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code for cheating and criminal conspiracy.
Rozak said all eight suspects had been remanded for three days from today until Aug 2 to facilitate investigations.
He added that police would intensify enforcement operations against illegal activities allegedly orchestrated by foreigners.

Title: Climbing legend Nirmal Purja among 10 missing after Pakistan avalanche
Article:
ISLAMABAD: Renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among 10 people missing after an avalanche in northern Pakistan where they were on a climbing expedition, the country's alpine club said.
"The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range," the club said late on Thursday, adding that the team led by Purja could not be reached since the incident.
The club said the expedition comprises 10 people – including five Nepalese, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American, a climber from China, and one other foreigner.
"The entire team has reportedly been out of communication since the avalanche," the club said.
Purja, 43, who served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide.
He climbed all 14 "eight-thousanders" (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 – then a record.
In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 along with a team of nine other Nepalese climbers.
- 'ASK FOR NOTHING' -
Purja wrote on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without oxygen.
"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.
"I take zero mountains for granted. Not one. The moment my foot leaves basecamp, it's 100%. Always has been. Always will be.
"My purpose has never been about me. It's about what I represent. It's about showing YOU that your own mountains – whatever they are – are climbable."
Broad Peak is the world's 12th highest mountain, located in the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000 metre-plus ascents.
It was first summited in 1957 by an Austrian team.
The Alpine Club said two Pakistan Army helicopters, carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment, have been sent to support the search operation.
"The helicopters are reinforcing efforts on the ground to assist the stranded climbers and enhance the effectiveness of the operation in the challenging high-altitude environment," the club said.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Stray dog dies during Port Klang capture operation after public interference
Article:
PORT KLANG: A stray dog died during a capture operation in Taman Teluk Gedung Indah after Majlis Bandaraya Diraja Klang personnel released the loop equipment being used following an incident involving members of the public.
The operation, carried out from 8.30pm to midnight on July 29, followed official complaints from residents over safety concerns linked to an increase in stray dogs in the area.
The council said in a statement that the operation involved 11 staff members, a Health Department officer and about 50 residents.
It said 12 stray dogs were captured using loop equipment that complied with standards set by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, with the process carried out while prioritising animal welfare.
The enforcement action was conducted under By-Law 17(1) of the MPK 2007 Dog Licensing and Dog Breeding Premises By-Laws.
However, during the operation at Jalan Sama Gagah 20, a group of individuals allegedly obstructed council personnel while they were attempting to capture a dog found roaming.
The council said one individual acted aggressively by attempting to cut the loop rope with a knife and threatened to harm himself if the animal was not released.
"The struggle and commotion that occurred disrupted the efforts of council personnel to loosen and release the equipment for the safety of the animal, resulting in the animal's death," it said.
Police later arrived at the scene to control the situation. The council said it had lodged a police report over the alleged obstruction of public personnel carrying out their duties and threats involving a sharp weapon.
The council said it remained committed to carrying out enforcement professionally and responsibly while complying with animal welfare standards.
Meanwhile, the Stray Animal Association of Malaysia said it had called for a thorough investigation into Rocky's death, alleging that the dog was beaten, strangled with a cable or wire, and dragged before dying during the incident.
In a statement, the association said Rocky was captured by a group of residents while his owner arrived when the dog was still alive but suffering.
The association also questioned the role of two council officers who were allegedly present at the scene.
It urged police to investigate those involved and called on the Selangor Veterinary Services Department to examine Rocky's remains to determine the cause of death.
The association said that any licensing issue should be handled through proper enforcement channels and not through actions that cause harm to animals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From recycled glass to miniature worlds: Syukur's terrarium passion blooms
Article:
JELI: A hobby of creating terrariums from recycled glass containers and second-hand items has blossomed into a creative passion for Muhammad Syukur Abdullah, 21, who now crafts intricate miniature garden landscapes.
The second-semester Aquaculture Technology Diploma student at Jeli Polytechnic said his interest began during his secondary school years after watching a YouTube video that inspired him to create his own terrarium.
"After several attempts with the help of online tutorials, I finally managed to create my first terrarium. My interest continued to grow, leading me to pursue an Aquaculture Technology Certificate at Jerantut Community College, Pahang, in 2022," he told Bernama at Jeli Polytechnic yesterday.
The Bukit Mertajam, Penang native said his two years at the community college provided him with valuable knowledge on plant care and maintenance, while his five-month industrial training at Gardenroad Aquatic in Shah Alam, Selangor, further strengthened his terrarium-making skills.
He began selling his creations on a small scale in 2022 through Facebook and Marketplace platforms.
Syukur said his passion continued after enrolling at Jeli Polytechnic, where he established the Green Vista Club under the guidance of Aquaculture Technology lecturer Zalina Che Manan to encourage students to share their interest and knowledge in the field.
[[nid:1501143]]
"We not only create terrariums but also share knowledge on planting and caring for plants in glass containers, including with kindergarten teachers," he said, adding that his terrariums are priced between RM10 and RM570 each.
He has mastered three types of terrarium designs – waterless landscapes, aquascapes featuring underwater environments, and paludariums combining terrestrial and aquatic elements such as waterfall designs.
He said the process begins with preparing several layers, including clay balls and black soil mixed with dry moss to maintain humidity.
"The base layer helps store water and allows plants to grow well. Once completed, I begin designing the terrarium using materials such as wood, stones and moss," he said, adding that spiderwood is among his preferred materials due to its durability and resistance to mould.
Syukur said arranging fine details remained the most challenging part, as each element must be carefully positioned to preserve the natural appearance of the miniature landscape.
He commonly uses plants such as fittonia, ferns and bonsai, with designs ranging from forest-inspired concepts and dioramas to Japanese and Iwagumi styles.
"Many customers prefer the diorama style because it resembles a fantasy world. Every terrarium is monitored for one to two weeks to ensure the plants adapt well before delivery," said the owner of the TikTok account syukx._.
He produces between five and 10 terrariums a month, with sizes ranging from mini and standard to premium. Production time varies from an hour to a day depending on the complexity of each design.
Syukur said terrariums required regular monitoring of humidity and lighting, with watering usually carried out once or twice a week depending on conditions.
Balancing studies with customer orders remained his biggest challenge, he said, adding that he carefully managed his time to meet deadlines.
He has yet to offer nationwide delivery as he remains concerned that the delicate creations could be damaged during transit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police receive 87 reports, open 23 investigation papers in Negeri Sembilan election campaign
Article:
SEREMBAN, July 31 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) received 87 reports and opened 23 investigation papers involving alleged election offences during the campaign period for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election from July 18 until yesterday.
Negeri Sembilan Police Chief DCP Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said 761 out of 787 permit applications submitted for ceramah and political campaign activities during the same period were approved.
“All political programmes and activities held are monitored to ensure they comply with the law and do not disrupt public safety and order,” he said in a statement here today.

He urged the public to continue complying with the law, respecting the democratic process and extending full cooperation to the police to ensure the election is conducted in a peaceful, harmonious and orderly manner.

Title: Anwar sends well‑wishes to Sultan Ibrahim ahead of medical treatment
